cases.title: A policy became recurring input
cases.intent: Preserve hard-won routing, custody, recovery and spending lessons across successive agents.
cases.mechanism: Current rules, historical incidents and project particulars accumulated in a central document. A full startup read made all of those layers recurring input.
cases.measured: 45,918 → 5,755 bytes; 26 original sections retained. The difference is 40,163 bytes per full load, or 87.47%.
cases.change: One current operating policy governs common behavior; project facts and historical reasons remain separately retrievable.
cases.state: Document change verified; task-speed benefit unmeasured
cases.retain: Custody, spending limits, original reasons, project acceptance and actual user authority.
cases.analogue: A temporary buffer, supplier exception or approval route remains active after its original conditions change.
cases.action: Attach applicability conditions, an accountable owner and a review trigger to each active rule, then compare matched tasks before and after the intake change.
cases.accept: Same task, source and runtime; record total wall time, input volume, tools, failures and accepted result. Preserve protections in both runs.
cases.failure: A smaller prompt with a worse or unverified result does not pass.

cases.title: The status surface concealed failure
cases.intent: Return a structured result so a parent could inspect a worker outcome.
cases.mechanism: The wrapper emitted a successful process exit even when its inner worker failed. A caller using only that outer signal could advance the wrong state.
cases.measured: W01: outer 0 / inner 1. N01: outer 0 / inner −9. The amendment maps completed → 0, usage unavailable → 1, failed → 1.
cases.change: The wrapper now propagates an unsuccessful outcome. Reporting is repaired; the failed work remains failed.
cases.retain: Original failed invocations, diagnostic results and the spending boundary.
cases.analogue: A meeting action is marked complete while the PO or production schedule still carries the previous quantity.
cases.action: Bind completion to the downstream receipt that actually discharges the commitment, and preserve reporting success separately from operating success.
cases.accept: A parent must refuse success for each failed child state; an actual completed child must still pass.
cases.failure: Submission, a green slide, or an exit wrapper alone cannot discharge an execution obligation.

cases.title: A good control met a changed operating condition
cases.intent: Bound spending, count cached input and stop work when usage could not be observed.
cases.mechanism: A reviewed two-second missing-usage rule later stopped cold-entry work after commentary, before any tool execution. The compatibility assumption became consequential.
cases.measured: The earlier 60,000-token threshold stopped at 83,374: 23,374 tokens of response-boundary overshoot. The later W01 attempt lasted 62.36 seconds and made zero tool calls.
cases.change: The reset retains accounting protections and exposes telemetry failure. It does not demonstrate a repaired inference path.
cases.retain: Inclusive accounting, finite limits, invocation identity and independent usage evidence.
cases.analogue: A finance or procurement control still assumes a reporting cadence that its source system no longer supplies.
cases.action: Qualify the meter against the actual runtime event contract in an isolated test; keep spending protections and preserve the failed trace.
cases.accept: A fresh worker completes useful work with independently observed usage, correct exit reporting and unchanged approved spending limits.
cases.failure: Relaxing the guard, bypassing accounting or calling missing data zero would conceal the problem.

cases.title: Assurance work lost its stopping condition
cases.intent: Protect a degraded source during a large data migration with copy, stream, coverage and hash checks.
cases.mechanism: A finisher scheduled another large-file rehash after accepted evidence already existed. The procedure kept executing after the decision could be closed.
cases.measured: 965,090 small files already verified. Rehash began 09:27; the 10:14 counter showed 296 GB. The operator stopped it at 10:26: a 59-minute recorded interval.
cases.change: The rule now admits the existing acceptance package and reserves rereads for an observed defect that justifies them.
cases.retain: Named residuals, coverage, copy summaries and verified stream evidence.
cases.analogue: Repeated inventory reconciliation or a quality hold continues after the accepted release evidence exists.
cases.action: Give each assurance obligation an explicit terminal condition and reuse the accepted receipt until a relevant input changes.
cases.accept: An unchanged, valid receipt discharges its scoped obligation; changed source identity or a real defect reopens it.
cases.failure: 59 minutes is observed elapsed time, not a measured promise of 59 minutes saved on every future job.

cases.title: An invisible dependency inherited a short lifetime
cases.intent: Carry a migration across an authenticated transport while retaining checkpoints.
cases.mechanism: The transport belonged to an interactive agent process. Its restart removed a dependency from work that was supposed to continue independently.
cases.measured: The 00:32 observation recorded 0 MB/s and 328 retries in the preceding hour. The controller account reports about 327,000 network-path error lines.
cases.change: The resulting rule assigns transfer dependencies to a task or service rather than the conversational process.
cases.retain: Pinned endpoints, checkpoints and the existing transfer owner.
cases.analogue: A supplier interface depends on a buyer’s session, private spreadsheet or unattended mailbox.
cases.action: Expose the dependency owner and required lifetime in the commitment; test owner restart with a disposable transfer.
cases.accept: A controlled session loss preserves the service-owned dependency and resumes from the same checkpoint without duplicate side effects.
cases.failure: A rule saying service-owned is not itself proof of restart resilience.

cases.title: The queue preserved objects without classifying work
cases.tier: Queue-derived figures in retained controller account
cases.intent: Preserve the content of a failing storage environment.
cases.mechanism: Regenerable caches and build environments entered the same small-file workflow as irreplaceable records.
cases.measured: 826,726 of 2,188,321 small files were build, environment or cache artifacts: 37.78% of the recorded queue.
cases.change: Triage distinguishes regenerable environments, repository bundles, historical holds and source material.
cases.state: Classification recorded; original queue unavailable here
cases.retain: Irreplaceable data, recovery evidence and explicit deletion authority.
cases.analogue: An inventory plan treats every unit as equivalent even though criticality, replenishment and obsolescence differ.
cases.action: Carry recovery class and regeneration cost into work admission, without deleting historical material merely because it is reproducible.
cases.accept: A sample of the regenerable class rebuilds correctly; independently measured transfer work falls while required recovery coverage remains.
cases.failure: A queue share is not a measured runtime or cash saving.

cases.title: Different snapshots looked like a contradiction
cases.intent: Keep recurring project instructions useful as work advanced.
cases.mechanism: Prompts accumulated operating history, while another task updated MARY concurrently. Counts without population and time mixed distinct states.
cases.measured: Eight changed prompts: 97,304 → 39,829 characters at apply. Later readback: 42,095 after an owner update. Ten active tasks is a different population.
cases.change: Shared policy is referenced once; project state stays with its owner. Apply and later-readback versions both remain.
cases.retain: Schedules, enabled states, project objectives and the subsequent owner’s update.
cases.analogue: Sales, Finance and Procurement answer using different forecast revisions or reporting periods.
cases.action: Bind every comparison to entity, population, version, effective time and observation time before asking which value is correct.
cases.accept: A reconciliation explains each difference using the correct source version, or opens a specific missing-evidence question.
cases.failure: An intentional later revision must not be classified as a failed earlier deployment.

cases.title: Authorship did not reveal the deployment surface
cases.intent: Make local entry points and project instructions useful to each worker.
cases.mechanism: Shared instructions were copied into roots, roles, generators, hooks and memory surfaces. An owner could approve each change without seeing its combined reach.
cases.measured: 570 recorded changes affected 555 unique targets across six hosts, retained in 22 receipts. Fifteen extra entries are amendments, not extra targets.
cases.change: Common policy has one owner; project entries preserve local facts and point to the current policy.
cases.retain: Every amendment, before/after digest and project-specific obligation.
cases.analogue: An approved planning change must propagate into forecast, PO, allocation, production and accounting systems.
cases.action: Compile the dependency and deployment set from the decision, then require readback at each affected boundary.
cases.accept: Every declared consumer reports the intended version, or remains explicitly outstanding; historical backups do not regain live authority.
cases.failure: Editing the source of truth alone does not establish propagation.

cases.title: Simplification needed to preserve the reason for the rule
cases.tier: Retained native configuration and AST checks
cases.intent: Protect permissions, quotas, resources, project evidence and custody.
cases.mechanism: Stale prose and valid executable controls occupied adjacent files. A broad cleanup could otherwise erase the protection along with the clutter.
cases.measured: The final-pass record reports 24 unchanged configurations and 15 hook-message sources revised with non-string AST preservation.
cases.change: Instruction text changed while protected runtime settings and project obligations remained.
cases.retain: Permissions, metadata, resource reservations, spending and project acceptance.
cases.analogue: A faster approval path must preserve credit exposure, quality constraints and contractual limits.
cases.action: Declare preserved invariants before migration; check them independently after the change.
cases.accept: The changed behavior meets its target and every retained invariant passes on actual deployed bytes.
cases.failure: Removing an inconvenient protection is a changed risk decision, not a free efficiency gain.

cases.title: Historical evidence and current authority needed separate states
cases.tier: Retained source and off-host copy receipts
cases.intent: Retain operational history so work and recovery survive individual sessions.
cases.mechanism: The same preserved text could be retrieved as evidence or misread as a present order. Erasing it would destroy the reasons needed for correction.
cases.measured: A 439-file source snapshot, 4,038,374 uncompressed bytes, and a 653,688-byte off-host bundle were retained; shared HEAD and index stayed unchanged.
cases.change: Historical material remains inspectable while current instructions determine execution.
cases.retain: Original statements, superseded versions, failed attempts and recovery coordinates.
cases.analogue: Old price agreements and forecasts must remain auditable without becoming today’s purchase authority.
cases.action: Store validity and supersession explicitly so historical retrieval cannot silently reactivate a retired instruction.
cases.accept: Replay retrieves the old reason and its measured consequences while present execution selects the current authorized rule.
cases.failure: The current corpus lacks one declared historical receipt digest; preserve that gap rather than reconstruct its bytes.
